question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 30 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 18 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (Capacity) = LCM of (12, 30, 18) = 180 units.

Combined efficiency = (180 ÷ 12) + (180 ÷ 30) + (180 ÷ 18) = 15 + 6 + 10 = 31 units/hour.

Time taken by A, B, and C together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 180 ÷ 31.

180 ÷ 31 = 5 25/31 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 25/31 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 12 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 30 hours

Time taken by Pipe C = 18 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken by individual pipes.

Combined Time = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 12
 180
 180 ÷ 12 = 15
 
 

 B
 30
 180 ÷ 30 = 6
 
 

 C
 18
 180 ÷ 18 = 10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 15 + 6 + 10 = 31 units/hour

⇒ Time taken by all three pipes together = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 180 ÷ 31

⇒ Time taken = 5 25/31 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 25/31 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Rule

If an inlet pipe can fill a tank in x hours, then the part of the tank filled in 1 hour is 1/x. This acts as positive efficiency.

Outlet Pipe Rule

If an outlet pipe empties a full tank in y hours, its 1 hour work is taken as negative i.e., −1/y.

Net Work Done

If both inlet and outlet pipes are opened together, the net 1 hour work is given by (1/x) − (1/y).
